headline_fact: A fallen leaf still takes part in the living world.
summary: Decomposing organisms break down dead plant material and help return its nutrients to the surrounding system.
did_you_know: Decomposing organisms break down dead plant material and help return its nutrients to the surrounding system.
core_mechanics: Decomposing organisms break down dead plant material and help return its nutrients to the surrounding system.
why_it_matters: Connect fallen leaves, decomposing organisms and nutrients in the soil.

in_depth_breakdown.real_world_application: These fungi are examples of organisms that take part in decomposition.

learning_takeaways: Dead leaves remain part of the natural system.
Decomposition connects dead material with available nutrients.

visual_suggestions.overview: Conceptual illustration of leaf litter and its connection to the soil, no labels, invented measurements or microscopic anatomy.

share_text: A fallen leaf still takes part in the living world.

image_details.alt: Conceptual illustration of leaf litter above soil
image_details.caption: Illustration: fallen leaves remain connected to the surrounding system.
image_details.learning_purpose: Connect dead material with the soil below.

identity.name: What happens to fallen leaves?
identity.scope: A general explanation of leaf-litter decomposition.

nature_lesson.hook: A fallen leaf still takes part in the living world.
nature_lesson.question: Where do the fallen leaves go?
nature_lesson.learning_goal: Connect fallen leaves, decomposing organisms and nutrients in the soil.

opening_observation.title: Look at the ground beneath a tree
opening_observation.scene: Fallen leaves collect on the ground. Some remain whole; others appear as fragments.
opening_observation.question: What changes this material after it falls?

nature_lesson.central_idea: Decomposing organisms break down dead plant material and help return its nutrients to the surrounding system.

explanation_status.explanation: Decomposition is well established. One view of the ground does not reveal its full history.

observation_context.where: On ground with fallen leaves, including woodland floors.
conditions: Fallen plant material and a soil community are present.
observation_context.size_context: Whole leaves are visible without tools. Many organisms involved are microscopic.
observation_context.time_context: A single visit cannot establish the rate of decomposition.
observation_context.variability: Different materials and soil communities produce different outcomes.

recognition_features.name: A layer of fallen leaves
recognition_features.what_to_look_for: Notice the leaves that rest on the ground.
recognition_features.meaning: This is leaf litter, a source of dead plant material.
recognition_features.connection: It supplies material for decomposing organisms.

recognition_features.name: Leaves in different states
recognition_features.what_to_look_for: Compare whole leaves with smaller fragments in a photograph.
recognition_features.meaning: Their condition offers clues, but not a complete explanation.
recognition_features.connection: A visible change does not identify its cause by itself.

key_terms.meaning: The breakdown of dead organic material.

explanation_steps.title: Leaves reach the ground
explanation_steps.explanation: Dead leaves become part of the leaf litter: plant material on the ground.
explanation_steps.what_changes: Material moves from the plant to the ground.
explanation_steps.evidence_note: This is the starting material, not proof of its decay rate.

explanation_steps.title: Organisms break down the material
explanation_steps.explanation: Fungi and bacteria digest dead plant material. Other soil organisms also take part in its breakdown.
explanation_steps.what_changes: The leaf material breaks down into simpler forms.
conditions: Decomposing organisms can reach the material.
explanation_steps.evidence_note: A photograph alone cannot identify all the organisms involved.

explanation_steps.title: Nutrients become available again
explanation_steps.explanation: Breakdown helps return nutrients to the soil, where plants can use them.
explanation_steps.what_changes: Nutrients in dead material rejoin the surrounding system.
conditions: Nutrient availability also depends on the local soil community.
explanation_steps.evidence_note: This describes a general process, not a measurement at this site.

diagram.title: From fallen leaf to available nutrients
diagram.caption: Follow the material through the process.
diagram.description: The links describe changes in material. They do not measure a rate.
assumptions: This summary leaves out many organisms and intermediate changes.

nodes.explanation: Material moves from the plant to the ground.
The leaf material breaks down into simpler forms.
Nutrients in dead material rejoin the surrounding system.

edges.label: Supplies material
edges.explanation: Dead leaves provide material for breakdown.

edges.label: Returns nutrients
edges.explanation: Breakdown helps make nutrients available again.

natural_connections.title: The connection to growing plants
natural_connections.relationship: Dead material links to new growth.
natural_connections.explanation: Plants use nutrients from their surroundings. Decomposition helps replenish that supply.
natural_connections.scale_or_conditions: This is a general connection, not a claim about one particular leaf.

real_world_example.title: Decomposing fungi at Mount Rainier
real_world_example.subject: Fungi that digest dead organic matter
real_world_example.place: Mount Rainier National Park, United States
real_world_example.observation: The park describes fungi that obtain nutrients from dead leaves, needles and wood.
real_world_example.explanation: These fungi are examples of organisms that take part in decomposition.
real_world_example.connection: Their activity connects dead plant material to nutrient cycling.
real_world_example.limits: This account does not identify a fungus in your own photograph.

notice_it_yourself.title: Compare without disturbing
notice_it_yourself.setting: Use a photograph of leaf litter.
steps: Find a whole leaf in the image.
Compare it with smaller fragments nearby.
notice_it_yourself.what_to_notice: Separate what you can see from what you infer.
notice_it_yourself.can_conclude: The photograph contains material in different visible states.
notice_it_yourself.cannot_conclude: You cannot infer its age, decay rate or exact decomposing organisms.
notice_it_yourself.care_note: Leave living organisms and the leaf layer undisturbed.

variation_and_limits.title: One photograph has limits
variation_and_limits.explanation: A still image records appearance. It does not establish how fast the material changes.

misconceptions.correction: Their material changes and moves through the surrounding system.
misconceptions.explanation: Breakdown returns nutrients rather than making matter vanish.

optional_depth.title: Why the whole soil community matters
optional_depth.explanation: Different soil organisms use different food sources. Their interactions affect nutrient availability.

knowledge_checks.question: Does a broken leaf identify the organism that broke it down?
knowledge_checks.explanation: The visible fragment is an observation. Its cause needs more evidence.

takeaways: Dead leaves remain part of the natural system.
Decomposition connects dead material with available nutrients.
